lens: PII leakage — does any PII (emails, phones, IBAN/cards, names) reach persisted turn content unredacted; detector.rs PII coverage vs guard_text usage; turn-read exposure gating

findings.issue: guard_text only detects EMAILS. Phone numbers, IBANs, credit-card numbers, SSNs, postal addresses and any free-form 'names' are NEVER detected or redacted. The comment at ingest_guard.rs:97 admits 'Extended (phone/IBAN/card) later'. Meanwhile prompts.rs:164 tells downstream agents Altevra '- Redact PII (emails, phone numbers, addresses, financial info)' — a false guarantee. Per the vision (CLAUDE.md §3.1) Altevra ingests health, relationship, finance and family data; the single PII detector covers only one of those vectors.
findings.leak_vector: A hook-captured turn like 'call Elena at +381 64 123 4567, IBAN RS35260005601001611379, card 4111 1111 1111 1111' passes guard_text untouched (no email present -> redaction_status=Clean) and is persisted verbatim into turns.content, then served raw to any AI via MCP search_turns/replay_session.
findings.fix: Add phone (E.164 + national formats), IBAN (with mod-97 checksum), payment-card (with Luhn) and optionally SSN detectors to detector.rs (new SecretKind/PII-kind variants) OR a dedicated pii.rs module, and call them inside guard_text after the email pass, pushing RiskTag::ThirdPartyPii and raising sensitivity. Until then, change prompts.rs:164 to stop claiming phone/address/financial redaction.

findings.issue: The OpenAI detector regex `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}` cannot match the CURRENT default OpenAI key formats `sk-proj-...`, `sk-svcacct-...`, `sk-admin-...`. After `sk-` the character class `[A-Za-z0-9]` halts at the hyphen following `proj`/`svcacct`, so only 4-7 alphanumerics are seen, below the {20,} minimum -> NO MATCH. Verified: regex.search('sk-proj-<redacted-example-key>...') => None. (Anthropic's regex at :67 correctly includes `_\-`, so sk-ant works; OpenAI's does not.)
findings.leak_vector: A modern OpenAI project/service key pasted into a prompt or tool arg is NOT detected by detect_secrets, so guard_text does not redact it and auto_capture does not vault it. The live API key persists in plaintext in turns.content and is later exposed verbatim through MCP replay_session/search_turns. This is a credential leak, the strongest class the gate claims to stop (R12-INV: secret=0 raw must never persist).
findings.fix: Change the openai pattern to allow the modern shape, e.g. `sk-(proj|svcacct|admin)?-?[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}` (or a dedicated alternation `sk-proj-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}` etc.), keeping the sk-ant exclusion. Add a regression test in detector.rs tests with a real-shaped `sk-proj-...` and `sk-svcacct-...` value.

findings.issue: Only the `content` column is run through guard_text/redact. The `tool_calls` JSON (raw tool_input) and `file_changes` JSON are persisted UNSCANNED in all three write paths. Tool inputs and file diffs are the single richest source of PII and secrets (Edit/Write payloads, Bash commands with `export OPENAI_API_KEY=...`, emails/IBANs in file contents, customer PII in WebFetch/SQL args).
findings.leak_vector: A PostToolUse hook for an Edit tool carries the full new file text (with a modern sk-proj- key or a customer email/phone) inside tool_input. record_turn copies it verbatim into turns.tool_calls. session.rs:333 (replay --json) and the MCP layer can return tool_calls raw. The guard_text on `content` is bypassed because the sensitive data lives in a sibling column that is never scanned.
findings.fix: Before persisting, deep-scan the tool_calls and file_changes JSON: serialize to string, run detect_secrets+PII redaction (or recurse over string leaves applying redact_with/guard_text), and store the redacted JSON. Bump redacted_count and risk_tags accordingly. Apply the SAME treatment in hook_handle.rs record_turn, analyze/orchestrator.rs import loop, and turn.rs.

findings.issue: The read/exposure surface for turns (MCP replay_session, search_turns; also CLI session.rs replay) reads turns directly via SessionsRepository::list_turns / search_turns and returns content/snippet with NO ExposureGate call, NO sensitivity ceiling, NO domain scope, NO redaction-status check. ExposureGate is only wired into the object-packet compiler (packet/mod.rs:105), which operates on object_index envelopes, NOT on turns.
findings.leak_vector: Any AI tool with MCP access calls search_turns('Elena') or replay_session and receives turn content/tool_calls regardless of how sensitive it is. Because turns are never gated, even correctly-classified-as-Restricted personal/health content (if classification existed) would be exposed; combined with the write-time gaps above, raw PII flows straight out. The exposure-gate invariant (single read path, fail-closed) is entirely unenforced for the highest-volume data type.
findings.fix: Route turn reads through ExposureGate: construct an Envelope (sensitivity+domains+redaction_status) per turn and call ExposureGate::decide with the caller's ExposureRequest before returning content; drop/deny turns above ceiling or insufficiently redacted. Requires the sensitivity/redaction columns from the next finding.

findings.location: crates/altevra-db/migrations/008_sessions_turns.sql:30-46 (turns table) vs crates/altevra-cli/src/commands/hook_handle.rs:195-205 (guarded.sensitivity computed then discarded); TurnRow at crates/altevra-db/src/repositories/sessions.rs:43-49
findings.issue: The `turns` table has NO `sensitivity` and NO `redaction_status` column (unlike objects in 020_relations_objects.sql, wiki 018, events 001). guard_text computes guarded.sensitivity (default-up) and guarded.redaction_status, but record_turn throws both away — only an integer redacted_count is stored. So a turn's classification is unrecoverable at read time, making fail-closed ceiling enforcement impossible.
findings.leak_vector: Even if turn reads were gated (previous finding), there is no persisted sensitivity to compare against the ceiling and no redaction_status to enforce min_redaction. The reader cannot distinguish a Clean turn from one that should have been Restricted, so it defaults to exposing everything (default-DOWN, violating the fail-closed invariant).
findings.fix: New migration (e.g. 025_turns_safety.sql) adding `sensitivity TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'restricted'` (fail-closed default UP, not 'internal') and `redaction_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unscanned'` to turns. Persist guarded.sensitivity.to_string() and guarded.redaction_status in record_turn (hook_handle.rs, turn.rs, orchestrator.rs). Extend TurnRow + INSERT/SELECT in sessions.rs.

findings.issue: Two write paths use the secrets-only `redact()` instead of `guard_text()`. `redact()` runs detect_secrets only — it performs NO PII (email) redaction at all and does NOT raise sensitivity. So imported sessions (analyze/Analyze-Everything) and manual `altevra turn record` persist emails (and all other PII) into turns.content unredacted, even though the live hook path was fixed to use guard_text.
findings.leak_vector: Importing Claude/Codex/Cursor/Hermes history (the primary bulk-ingest path described in CLAUDE.md §3.5) stores every email in every historical turn in plaintext. turn.rs additionally exposes a `--no-redact` flag (turn.rs:78-79) that stores fully raw content with redacted_count=0.
findings.fix: Replace redact() with guard_text(&turn.content, Sensitivity::Internal) in orchestrator.rs:271 and turn.rs:81-84, persisting the resulting value+sensitivity+redaction_status. Remove or gate the `--no-redact` flag behind an explicit Pavle-authorized env so it cannot silently bypass PII scrubbing.

findings.issue: AWS detector only matches long-term `AKIA` keys. Temporary STS access keys begin with `ASIA` (and other AWS id prefixes exist); `ASIA1234567890ABCDEF` is NOT matched. Verified: regex.search('ASIA1234567890ABCDEF') => None.
findings.leak_vector: A temporary AWS session credential (ASIA...) pasted in a prompt/tool arg is not detected, not redacted, not vaulted; persists raw in turns.content and is exposed via MCP.
findings.fix: Broaden the prefix: `(AKIA|ASIA|AROA|AIDA|ANPA|AGPA)[0-9A-Z]{16}` (at minimum add ASIA), with a regression test.

findings.location: crates/altevra-secrets/src/ingest_guard.rs:98-127 (detect_emails) — no-dot domain miss and trailing-dot over-capture; unicode local-part truncation
findings.issue: The hand-rolled email scanner (1) requires `saw_dot` in the domain, so intranet/mailbox forms like `john@localhost`, `pavle@mailserver` are MISSED (no redaction); (2) over-consumes a trailing dot (`x@y.com.` captures the trailing '.', cosmetic); (3) on a unicode local part `jöhn@x.com` it only walks back over ASCII so it truncates rather than fully covering the local part (verified: captures 'n@x.com', leaving 'jöh' — a partial-identity leak and shows the ASCII-only walk-back is fragile).
findings.leak_vector: Internal/dotless email addresses and unicode-prefixed addresses are not fully redacted, leaking partial or full PII into persisted turn content.
findings.fix: Replace the ad-hoc scanner with a vetted email regex (anchored local@domain with proper TLD/host handling, unicode-aware), or relax the saw_dot requirement for known hostless forms and trim trailing punctuation. Add tests for dotless, trailing-dot, and unicode-local cases.

findings.issue: Coverage gaps in adjacent credential shapes: Slack app-level tokens `xapp-...` are out of the `xox[bpars]` class; `redis://user:pass@`, `amqp://`, `mssql://`, generic `://user:pass@` URLs are not in the db_url alternation; Google API keys `AIza...` and Stripe `sk_live_/rk_live_` (underscore, not hyphen) match nothing. These are credentials, not strictly PII, but they ride the same unredacted persist path.
findings.leak_vector: These credential shapes persist raw in turns.content/tool_calls and are exposed via MCP, same as the OpenAI gap.
findings.fix: Extend patterns: slack `xox[bpars]|xapp` ; db_url add `redis|amqp|mssql|mariadb` and a generic `://[^:@\s]+:([^@\s]+)@` fallback; add Google `AIza[0-9A-Za-z_\-]{35}` and Stripe `(sk|rk)_(live|test)_[0-9A-Za-z]{20,}` detectors. Add regression tests.

invariants_checked: R12-INV (secret=0/scope=0/sensitivity=0 raw must NEVER persist): VIOLATED — modern OpenAI sk-proj keys (detector.rs:66) and AWS ASIA creds (detector.rs:68) evade detection and persist raw; tool_calls/file_changes columns persist raw in all write paths (hook_handle.rs:225-245, orchestrator.rs:279, turn.rs:106-112).

PII coverage (emails/phones/IBAN/cards/names): VIOLATED — guard_text detects emails only (ingest_guard.rs:97-128); phone/IBAN/card/SSN/address never detected despite prompts.rs:164 claiming they are redacted.

fail-closed: unscanned/unknown -> max sensitivity: PARTIALLY VIOLATED — Sensitivity::Other ranks max (security.rs:49) correctly, but turns have no sensitivity/redaction_status columns (008_sessions_turns.sql) and guard_text's computed sensitivity is discarded on persist (hook_handle.rs:195), so reads default-DOWN (everything exposable) instead of UP.

exposure_gate is the single read path: VIOLATED for turns — ExposureGate is only applied in packet/mod.rs:105 over object_index; MCP replay_session/search_turns (tools_sessions.rs:44-111) and CLI session replay (session.rs:328-340) read turn content/tool_calls with no gate.

exposure_gate ceiling math touches only sensitivity_level (R1-INV): HOLDS — exposure_gate.rs:109-114 uses within_ceiling (rank-only); security.rs within_ceiling/combine are level-only and monotone-max. No wrong-field/wrong-operator found in the gate itself.

deny reasons do not leak existence of higher-sensitivity objects: HOLDS — DenyReason::code() (exposure_gate.rs:73-80) returns coarse strings (items_above_ceiling_omitted etc.) with no count/type; verified by personal_health_excluded_from_work_packet test.

TAG-1 (untagged write -> quarantine): HOLDS for templated ingest_guard path (ingest_guard.rs:238-241 via TemplateGate; untagged_write_is_quarantined test) — BUT NOT APPLICABLE/ENFORCED on the turn path, which uses guard_text (no template/tag gate) and persists regardless.
Anthropic vs OpenAI overlap dedup: HOLDS — anthropic regex includes _- and runs first; sk-ant correctly classified (detector.rs:67,100-103; openai_does_not_swallow_anthropic test).

findings.issue: The live hook write path persists RAW, UNSCANNED payload fields. `tool_calls` is set to `payload.get("tool_input").cloned()` (lines 226 and 229) and `file_changes` to `payload.get("file_changes").cloned()` (line 245). Only `content` goes through guard_text; tool_input and file_changes never touch the detector/redactor. In handle_pre_tool_use the SAME tool_input is scanned into `content` (redacted) but then re-stored UNREDACTED in `tool_calls` on the identical row — a self-defeating bypass. The 008 migration comment claims 'what lands on disk is already clean' / 'tool args redacted' which is false.
findings.leak_vector: A real secret or PII sitting in a tool's arguments (e.g. a Bash command `export DATABASE_URL=postgres://u:pw@h/db`, an env dump, an API request body) or in a file diff (the single most common place real keys live) is written verbatim into turns.tool_calls / turns.file_changes / file_changes table. R12-INV: raw secret with no sensitivity/scope persists. It is then exposed by search_turns / replay / session read paths, none of which run ExposureGate on turns.
findings.fix: Route tool_input and file_changes through guard_text (or at minimum redact_with + detect_emails) BEFORE building TurnRow; store only the guarded value. Add an integration test that pipes a PostToolUse payload whose tool_input/file_changes contain sk-/ghp_/postgres:// + an email and asserts none of the raw values appear in any persisted column. files_to_edit: crates/altevra-cli/src/commands/hook_handle.rs. new_files: crates/altevra-cli/tests/hook_raw_payload_redaction.rs. cargo test -p altevra-cli --test hook_raw_payload_redaction

findings.location: crates/altevra-secrets/src/detector.rs:66 (openai regex) and the whole patterns() set:62-80
findings.issue: Detector misses the CURRENT-generation, real-shaped secrets. `openai: sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}` cannot match `sk-proj-...` or `sk-svcacct-...` (the default OpenAI key format since 2024) because the `-` after `sk-proj` breaks the [A-Za-z0-9]+ run at char 4. Stripe `sk_live_`/`sk_test_` (underscore, not dash) is missed entirely. `postgresql://` (the canonical full scheme name) is missed because db_url requires literal `postgres` immediately followed by `://`. `mongodb+srv://`, `redis://`, Google `AIza...`, SendGrid `SG.`, npm `npm_`, Twilio `AC...`/auth tokens, AWS 40-char secret-access-key, and `Authorization: Bearer ...` are all missed. Verified empirically against the exact regexes.
findings.leak_vector: A live OpenAI project key, Stripe live key (real money), or postgresql:// connection string in turn content returns ZERO matches → guard_text leaves matches.is_empty() true → value=body UNCHANGED, redaction_status=Clean, sensitivity stays Internal. Raw credential persists AND is classified DOWN as clean/internal (also violates fail-closed). It then passes the ExposureGate (Clean+Internal) and is handed to any work-scope reader.
findings.fix: Add/repair patterns: openai `sk-(proj|svcacct|admin)?-?[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}` plus a separate Stripe `sk_(live|test)_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}`; db_url scheme alternation `(postgres(ql)?|mysql|mongodb(\+srv)?|redis|amqps?)`; add Google AIza, SendGrid, npm, Twilio, generic Bearer. Each new kind needs is_hard_secret + secret_kind_label coverage. files_to_edit: crates/altevra-secrets/src/detector.rs (patterns + detect_secrets loops + SecretKind enum), crates/altevra-secrets/src/ingest_guard.rs (secret_kind_label, is_hard_secret), crates/altevra-secrets/src/capture.rs (derive_key_name). new_files: none. cargo test -p altevra-secrets detector

findings.issue: For DatabaseUrl the redacted span is the password capture group `[^@\s]+`, which stops at the FIRST `@`. When the password itself contains `@` (legal and common, e.g. `p@ssw0rd`), only the prefix before the first `@` is captured/redacted; the remainder of the password leaks. Verified: `postgres://user:p@sswithat@host/db` captures only `p`, leaving `sswithat` in the persisted text.
findings.leak_vector: A DB password containing `@` is partially exposed in stored turn content / wiki bodies — a credential-class (rejected) secret partially survives, contradicting the §2.5 promise that credentialed DB URLs are never stored.
findings.fix: Redact the whole `://user:PASSWORD@` credential segment (or anchor the password match to the LAST `@` before the host using a greedy `.+` up to `@host`), or treat any db_url match as full-line rejection rather than substring redaction. files_to_edit: crates/altevra-secrets/src/detector.rs:78. new_files: none. cargo test -p altevra-secrets detects_db_url_password_only (extend with @-in-password case)

findings.issue: The bulk-import path (Analyze Everything: cursor/hermes/codex/claude_code parsers → import_session) uses the OLD secrets-only `altevra_secrets::redact()` (line 271), NOT guard_text. So imported turn content has secrets stripped but PII (emails) is NOT redacted and sensitivity is NEVER classified. This is the exact regression the hook path comment at hook_handle.rs:191-194 calls out ('Previously only secrets were redacted; PII leaked into stored content') — the import path was never fixed. Additionally line 279 persists `turn.tool_calls.clone()` raw and unscanned.
findings.leak_vector: Importing existing Hermes/Codex/Cursor histories writes every third-party email and all tool-call arguments (which hold DB URLs, tokens, env dumps) into turns with no PII redaction and no sensitivity label. Mass PII/secret ingestion at import time, then exposed via search.
findings.fix: Replace redact() with guard_text() in the import loop and store guarded.value; scan/redact turn.tool_calls the same way; carry guarded.sensitivity onto the row. files_to_edit: crates/altevra-cli/src/commands/analyze/orchestrator.rs:265-289. new_files: crates/altevra-cli/tests/import_pii_redaction.rs. cargo test -p altevra-cli --test import_pii_redaction

findings.issue: PII detection is emails-ONLY. Phone numbers, IBANs, credit-card numbers, and national IDs are explicitly deferred ('Extended (phone/IBAN/card) later') and slip through completely. Worse, the sensitivity classifier only raises to Confidential on a hard secret or an email; it NEVER inspects domain/content for Health/Relationship/Financial/Legal personal data. A turn full of relationship or health text with no email and no secret is classified at the caller's default (Internal), i.e. DEFAULT-DOWN on exactly the data the vision marks Restricted.
findings.leak_vector: A turn like 'Elena's therapist said her diagnosis is X, phone +1-555-123-4567, IBAN RS3526000560100161137' carries no email and no secret → guard_text returns sensitivity=Internal, redaction_status=Clean, value unchanged. It then passes ExposureGate.default_work() (Internal ceiling) and leaks personal/health PII into a work-scope context packet. Violates fail-closed + personal-first parity.
findings.fix: Add phone/IBAN/card/national-id detectors to guard_text and a content/domain → sensitivity escalation (Health/Relationship/Financial/Legal risk tags must combine() UP to Restricted). At minimum, when domain.is_high_water() the body must be classified Restricted by default. files_to_edit: crates/altevra-secrets/src/ingest_guard.rs (detect_* + classify), crates/altevra-core/src/domain.rs (reuse is_high_water). new_files: crates/altevra-secrets/tests/pii_phone_iban_card.rs. cargo test -p altevra-secrets --test pii_phone_iban_card

findings.issue: The generic assignment detector only triggers on the keyword set `(api[-_]?key|secret|token)`. The most common credential keyword, `password`/`passwd`/`pwd`/`pass`, is absent, so `password=SuperSecretValue123456` returns no match. The value charset `[A-Za-z0-9_+/=\-]{20,}` also excludes `.`, so dotted secrets (many tokens) are truncated or missed. Verified empirically.
findings.leak_vector: A literal `password=...` / `pwd: ...` assignment in turn content or a tool command persists raw (Clean/Internal), bypassing the gate.
findings.fix: Extend the keyword alternation to include password|passwd|passphrase|pwd|pass|client[-_]?secret|access[-_]?token|auth and add `.` to the value charset. files_to_edit: crates/altevra-secrets/src/detector.rs:72-74. new_files: none. cargo test -p altevra-secrets detects_generic_api_key (extend with password= case)

findings.issue: github_pat hardcodes exactly 82 body chars; GitHub fine-grained PAT length is not contractually fixed and real tokens of other lengths (e.g. 76) are missed. github_prefix hardcodes exactly {36}; newer/longer classic tokens (40+) match only by luck of {36} being a prefix — a token shorter than 36 after the prefix is missed. Tight exact-length anchors make the detector brittle and miss real tokens.
findings.leak_vector: A GitHub token of a non-82 / non-36 body length persists raw.
findings.fix: Loosen to `github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{30,}` and `(ghp|gho|ghu|ghs|ghr)_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}` (lower-bounded, not exact). files_to_edit: crates/altevra-secrets/src/detector.rs:69-70. new_files: none. cargo test -p altevra-secrets detects_github_tokens

findings.location: crates/altevra-cli/src/commands/hook_handle.rs:175-182 and 199; turns table (008_sessions_turns.sql) has no redaction_status/sensitivity columns
findings.issue: Turns are persisted with NO redaction_status and NO sensitivity column — there is nowhere to record that a turn was scanned, so reads of turns cannot run the ExposureGate (which requires a RedactionStatus). guard_text raises sensitivity but the result (guarded.sensitivity) is DISCARDED — never stored. Also when no current session exists, record_turn silently returns Ok(()) (line 178-181) so an untagged write is dropped, not quarantined (TAG-1 says quarantine, not silent drop). redacted_count uses `captures.len().max(guarded.sightings.len())` which undercounts when both captures and sightings are non-empty-but-different, weakening audit.
findings.leak_vector: Because turns carry no sensitivity/redaction metadata, every downstream reader treats them as exposable. Combined with the raw-persist findings above, restricted content in turns is exposed with no gate. The silent-skip path means content can vanish without a quarantine record (no audit of a dropped untagged write).
findings.fix: Add redaction_status and sensitivity columns to turns (new migration 026_turn_safety_columns.sql), persist guarded.redaction_status + guarded.sensitivity, and make any turn read go through ExposureGate. Replace silent-skip with a quarantine record. Fix redacted_count to sum, not max. files_to_edit: crates/altevra-cli/src/commands/hook_handle.rs (TurnRow build + redacted_count), crates/altevra-db/src/repositories/* (TurnRow struct + insert/read). new_files: crates/altevra-db/migrations/026_turn_safety_columns.sql, crates/altevra-cli/tests/turn_exposure_gate.rs. cargo test -p altevra-cli --test turn_exposure_gate

findings.issue: After sort_by_key(start), the dedup keeps the EARLIEST-starting match and drops any later match that starts before prev.end. Because matches are appended per-kind in a fixed order (anthropic, openai, aws, ... generic, db_url) and the sort is not stable on equal start with longer-end preference, a shorter earlier-pushed match at the same start offset can win over a longer/more-specific one, redacting fewer bytes than the true secret span and leaving a tail in the text. The doc comment claims 'the longer / more specific match wins' but the code keeps first-by-start with no length tiebreak.
findings.leak_vector: In rare overlapping cases (e.g. a generic api_key= value whose captured group starts at the same offset as another pattern) the shorter span is chosen and the secret tail survives redaction.
findings.fix: After sort, on equal start prefer the match with the larger end (sort_by(|a,b| a.start.cmp(&b.start).then(b.end.cmp(&a.end)))), and when skipping an overlap, extend prev.end to max(prev.end, m.end). files_to_edit: crates/altevra-secrets/src/detector.rs:184-196. new_files: none. cargo test -p altevra-secrets (add overlapping_longer_match_wins test)

findings.location: crates/altevra-core/src/packet/mod.rs:105 (PacketCompiler::compile) + crates/altevra-db/migrations/020_relations_objects.sql:object_index table (no redaction_status column) + crates/altevra-core/src/safety/exposure_gate.rs:95-128 (decide signature takes redaction: Option<&RedactionStatus>)
findings.issue: The ExposureGate's redaction check (exposure_gate.rs step 4, lines 124-128) is structurally DEAD on the read/packet path. The packet compiler ALWAYS calls ExposureGate::decide(&c.envelope, None, &request.exposure) — passing None for redaction — so redaction_exposable() is never evaluated for any object that flows through a context packet. Compounding this: the object_index table (the compiler's only candidate source, objects.rs:189 candidates()) has NO redaction_status column at all (migration 020), and durable tables (learnings/insight_cards/memory_documents, migrations 019/020) default redaction_status to 'unscanned'. So an object whose body was never scanned (or was Quarantined/Rejected) but whose envelope is Internal/Business sails through the gate and is exposed.
findings.leak_vector: Write a learning/insight_card with redaction_status='unscanned' (the schema DEFAULT) containing a raw secret or health note in the body, domain=business, sensitivity=internal. It satisfies ceiling+scope+lifecycle. Because decide() is called with redaction=None, the fail-closed redaction branch never fires. The item is included in the packet and handed to whatever AI tool requested context. The invariant 'unscanned/unknown -> never default-down' and R12-INV 'unscanned raw must NEVER be exposed' are both violated.
findings.fix: 1) Add a redaction_status column to object_index (new migration, e.g. 026_object_index_redaction.sql: ALTER TABLE object_index ADD COLUMN redaction_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unscanned'); maintain it on every upsert. 2) Carry redaction_status on PacketCandidate (add field in packet/mod.rs PacketCandidate) and pass Some(&c.redaction_status) into ExposureGate::decide at packet/mod.rs:105 instead of None. 3) Make 'unscanned' fail-closed in redaction_exposable (it already is — only Clean|Redacted pass — but it must actually be fed the value). Acceptance: cargo test -p altevra-core packet::tests::unscanned_object_excluded_from_packet (new test asserting an Internal/Business candidate with Unscanned redaction is denied RedactionInsufficient).

findings.location: crates/altevra-secrets/src/detector.rs:66 (openai regex `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}`) and :78 (db_url regex `(postgres|mysql|mongodb)://...`); consumed by guard_text crates/altevra-secrets/src/ingest_guard.rs:148-205 and the live turn path crates/altevra-cli/src/commands/hook_handle.rs:195
findings.issue: Detector regex gaps let real-world credentials persist RAW. Proven against the actual `regex` crate: (a) OpenAI project keys `sk-proj-...` (the DEFAULT key format OpenAI issues since 2024) MISS, because after `sk-` the literal `proj` is only 4 alphanumerics before a `-`, failing `{20,}`; (b) the canonical Postgres scheme `postgresql://user:pw@host` MISSES because the alternation only lists `postgres`, not `postgresql`; (c) `password=`/`pwd=` assignments MISS because the generic keyword group is only `(api[-_]?key|secret|token)`; (d) Google `AIza...` keys, AWS STS temp keys `ASIA...`, and Slack webhook URLs (`hooks.slack.com/services/...`) have no detector at all.
findings.leak_vector: Pavle pastes `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-<64 chars>` or `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://app:hunter2@db/prod` or `password=<24+ chars>` into any Claude Code/Codex turn. record_turn (hook_handle.rs:195) calls guard_text, which calls detect_secrets, which returns empty -> RedactionStatus::Clean, sensitivity stays Internal, and the RAW value is written to turns.content (migration 008 comment line 7-9 explicitly relies on 'what lands on disk is already clean'). The secret is now durably stored unredacted AND will be exposed via any reader. R12-INV (secret=... raw must never persist) is violated.
findings.fix: In detector.rs patterns(): (a) change openai to also catch project/service keys, e.g. `sk-(proj|svcacct|admin)-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}` as a separate AnthropicKey-style early pattern, OR broaden to `sk-[A-Za-z0-9-]{20,}` while keeping the sk-ant- exclusion ordering; (b) change db_url scheme group to `(postgres|postgresql|mysql|mongodb|mongodb\+srv|redis|rediss|amqp)`; (c) add `password|passwd|pwd|pass|bearer` to the generic keyword group and also match `Authorization:\s*Bearer`; (d) add detectors for Google `AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}`, AWS `(AKIA|ASIA|AROA|AIDA)[0-9A-Z]{16}`, and Slack webhook `hooks\.slack\.com/services/[A-Za-z0-9/]+`. Acceptance: cargo test -p altevra-secrets detector (add positive tests for sk-proj-, postgresql://, password=, AIza, ASIA, slack webhook) and cargo test -p altevra-secrets ingest_guard::tests (assert guard_text redacts each and sets RedactionStatus::Redacted).

findings.location: crates/altevra-secrets/src/ingest_guard.rs:97-132 (detect_emails is the ONLY PII detector) and :185-189 (classify); live path crates/altevra-cli/src/commands/hook_handle.rs:195
findings.issue: PII detection is email-only (the code comment at line 97 admits 'Extended (phone/IBAN/card) later'). Phone numbers, IBANs, credit cards, SSNs, postal addresses, and names are NOT detected or redacted. Worse, even when PII (email) IS found, guard_text only bumps sensitivity to Confidential (combine with Sensitivity::Confidential, line 188), never to Restricted — the band the ladder reserves for 'Personal / relationship / health / legal / financial high-water mark' (security.rs:33). There is NO content classifier that raises health/relationship/financial prose to Restricted, and Domain::is_high_water (domain.rs:48) is used NOWHERE in exposure/packet gating (grep confirms zero call sites outside domain.rs).
findings.leak_vector: A turn or learning containing 'Elena's therapist phone is +381 64 123 4567, she's on sertraline for depression' is stored with sensitivity=Internal (no email, no secret -> no bump), redaction_status=Clean. A default_work() ExposureRequest (ceiling=Internal) then EXPOSES it to a work-context AI tool. The restricted health/relationship body never reaches the Restricted band, so the ceiling=Internal default never excludes it. Health/relationship leak into work packets — the exact primary leak the suite is meant to block.
findings.fix: 1) Add phone/IBAN/card/SSN regex detectors to the PII pass (or a new altevra-secrets/src/pii.rs). 2) Add a sensitivity classifier that raises to Restricted when health/relationship/financial/legal risk-tags or keywords are present, and have guard_text emit the matching RiskTag (Health/Relationship/Financial/Legal). 3) Make ingest_guard raise sensitivity to Restricted (not just Confidential) when domain.is_high_water() OR a high-water risk tag is set. Acceptance: cargo test -p altevra-secrets ingest_guard::tests::health_content_classified_restricted and ::phone_pii_redacted.

findings.location: crates/altevra-core/src/packet/mod.rs:62-67 (ExclusionRecord) and :110-116 (emit) — ExclusionRecord is part of the returned ContextPacket (struct field `excluded`, line 73) and persisted to context_packets.excluded (migration 022 line 19)
findings.issue: Existence/side-channel leak via exclusion records. When an item is denied for OverSensitivityCeiling (e.g. a Restricted health object), the compiler still pushes an ExclusionRecord carrying the real object_type and object_id of that hidden item into the packet's `excluded` list. exposure_gate.rs documents (lines 10-11, 57) that deny reasons must 'never reveal the existence, count, or type of a higher-classified item' — but DenyReason::code() only coarsens the REASON string; the surrounding ExclusionRecord still leaks the object's type and stable id. ContextPacket.exclusion_reason(id) (lines 82-87) lets a caller probe by id and learn that a hidden higher-sensitivity object with that exact id exists.
findings.leak_vector: An agent requesting a work packet receives `excluded: [{object_type:'learning', object_id:'l_health_elena_diagnosis', reason:'items_above_ceiling_omitted'}]`. The id/type themselves disclose the existence and topic of a Restricted object the caller is forbidden to see, plus an enumerable handle. Counts are 'exact' (migration 021 comment) which further confirms cardinality of hidden items.
findings.fix: For OverSensitivityCeiling (and any over-ceiling/out-of-scope deny on a higher-than-ceiling item), do NOT emit a per-object ExclusionRecord with type+id. Instead emit a single aggregate, content-free record (e.g. reason='items_above_ceiling_omitted' with no id, or an opaque non-enumerable token), and store the precise type/id ONLY in the non-exposed exposure_decisions audit (migration 021), never in the packet body returned to the caller. Acceptance: cargo test -p altevra-core packet::tests::over_ceiling_exclusion_has_no_object_id (assert the returned packet's excluded entries for over-ceiling items carry neither the real object_id nor object_type).

findings.location: crates/altevra-cli/src/commands/hook_handle.rs:167-251 (record_turn) — specifically :195-196 (guard_text result used) and :218-250 (turn persisted unconditionally); turns table migration 008 has no redaction_status column
findings.issue: The live turn-capture path persists guarded.value WITHOUT honoring the guard's safety verdict and WITHOUT a fail-closed flag. record_turn never inspects guarded.redaction_status, never checks an is_safe_to_persist gate, and the turns table has no redaction_status column (TurnRow, sessions.rs:36-54, has only redacted_count i64). So if guard_text returns Unscanned (it can't today, but any future detector error path) or simply MISSES a secret (see detector findings), the raw content is written with no durable marker that it was unscanned/insufficiently redacted — meaning a downstream reader cannot fail-closed on it either. The fail-closed posture asserted in ingest_guard.rs:5-8 is not enforced for the highest-volume write (turns).
findings.leak_vector: Combined with the detector gaps: a missed sk-proj-/postgresql:///password= secret is written to turns.content with redacted_count possibly 0 and no redaction_status, indistinguishable from genuinely clean content. Any later exposure of turn content (search, packet, import) treats it as safe.
findings.fix: 1) Add redaction_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unscanned' (and sensitivity) to the turns table (new migration 026) and to TurnRow. 2) In record_turn, set turn.redaction_status = guarded.redaction_status and turn.sensitivity = guarded.sensitivity. 3) Any read/exposure path over turns must run through ExposureGate with the real redaction_status. Acceptance: cargo test -p altevra-cli hook_handle::tests::turn_persists_redaction_status (assert a turn with a redacted secret stores redaction_status='redacted').

findings.location: crates/altevra-core/src/safety/exposure_gate.rs:20-42 (ExposureRequest.min_redaction declared, defaulted) vs :95-131 (decide never reads request.min_redaction; uses hardcoded redaction_exposable at :86-88)
findings.issue: The `min_redaction` policy field is dead. It is declared (line 26), documented as enforcing 'redaction_status >= min_redaction' (module doc line 6), and set in default_work() (line 38), but decide() never reads it — redaction is judged solely by the hardcoded redaction_exposable() (Clean|Redacted pass, everything else fails). A caller that tightens min_redaction (e.g. to require Clean-only, rejecting Redacted) gets NO effect; a caller that loosens it also gets no effect. This is a silent policy no-op: an operator believes they configured a stricter ceiling than is actually applied.
findings.leak_vector: An operator sets min_redaction=Clean expecting Redacted (placeholder-containing) items to be excluded from a high-sensitivity export. The field is ignored, so Redacted items (which may contain mis-redacted fragments from the gappy detector) are still exposed. The policy/actual-behavior divergence is itself a trust-violating fail-open relative to the configured intent.
findings.fix: Make decide() honor request.min_redaction: implement a total order on RedactionStatus (Unscanned < Redacted < Clean, with Quarantined/Rejected non-exposable) and gate with `redaction_rank(r) >= redaction_rank(&request.min_redaction)` instead of the hardcoded helper. Acceptance: cargo test -p altevra-core exposure_gate::tests::min_redaction_clean_excludes_redacted (set request.min_redaction=Clean, item Redacted -> Deny(RedactionInsufficient)).

findings.issue: Redundant/divergence-prone lifecycle logic. Line 101 enters the block when `!envelope.status.is_default_readable()`, which (status.rs:147) is true exactly when status is NOT Draft|Active. The inner guard at line 103 `if !matches!(envelope.status, ObjectStatus::Draft | ObjectStatus::Active)` is therefore ALWAYS true inside that block — dead code. Behavior today is correct and fail-closed (unknown ObjectStatus::Other also denies NotCurrent). But the readability rule is duplicated in two places (is_default_readable AND the inline matches!); a future edit to one and not the other could silently expose a status that one predicate treats as readable and the other does not.
findings.leak_vector: No live leak today. Latent: if someone adds a new readable status to is_default_readable() but the inline matches! at line 103 isn't updated (or vice versa), the gate could begin admitting a non-current object, or the two predicates could disagree, creating an exposure inconsistency that no test currently pins.
findings.fix: Remove the redundant inner matches! and rely on the single source of truth: `if !request.include_history && !envelope.status.is_default_readable() { return Deny(NotCurrent); }`. Keep one readability predicate. Acceptance: cargo test -p altevra-core exposure_gate::tests::all_non_default_statuses_denied (table test over ObjectStatus::known() minus Draft/Active plus an Other, all -> Deny(NotCurrent) without include_history).

invariants_checked: R1-INV (ceiling math touches only sensitivity_level): within_ceiling uses rank() comparison on the 6-ladder only — CORRECT in isolation (security.rs:64-66). Secret level has no durable body classification path — CORRECT. But the ceiling test is the only protection on the read path, and it is undermined by the dead redaction gate (finding 1) and by guard_text never raising personal/health content to Restricted (finding 3), so an Internal-default ceiling fails to exclude high-water personal data.

R12-INV (secret=0 raw must never persist/expose): VIOLATED — detector regex gaps (sk-proj-, postgresql://, password=, AIza, ASIA, slack webhook) let raw credentials persist into turns.content with redaction_status Clean/absent (findings 2,5).

TAG-1 (untagged write -> quarantine): HOLDS for templated ingest_guard path (TemplateGate.check defaults min_categories=1, quarantines untagged; ingest_guard.rs:235-241). BUT the high-volume guard_text/turn path (hook_handle.rs record_turn) does NOT run TemplateGate at all — turns are persisted with no category/quarantine gate; untagged turn content is silently stored.

Exposure deny reasons must not leak existence: VIOLATED — DenyReason::code() coarsens the reason string, but ExclusionRecord still carries the real object_type+object_id of over-ceiling hidden items into the returned packet body and exposure_reason() lookup (finding 4).

fail-closed (unscanned/unknown -> max sensitivity, never default-down): PARTIALLY HOLDS at the type level — Sensitivity::Other ranks u8::MAX (security.rs:49), ObjectStatus::Other denies NotCurrent. VIOLATED at the data level — durable tables default redaction_status='unscanned' yet the packet gate is fed redaction=None, so unscanned objects are NOT excluded (finding 1); and content with no detected secret/email defaults to Internal regardless of true sensitivity (finding 3).
min_redaction policy enforcement: VIOLATED — field is declared and defaulted but never read by decide() (finding 6), a silent fail-open relative to configured policy.

ExposureGate ceiling-before-scope ordering (no domain existence leak via reason): HOLDS — ceiling (line 109) is checked before domain scope (line 117), so an over-ceiling item denies OverSensitivityCeiling rather than revealing it was out-of-scope/which domain.

PacketCandidate<-ObjectIndexRow wiring: NOT WIRED — no conversion exists in the codebase from ObjectIndexRow/DB rows to PacketCandidate; the 'single read/exposure path' is not connected to storage in P0.1, so the gate is currently only unit-tested, not enforced on real reads (structural gap underlying findings 1 and 4).
